STEP 1 - Scene: A breakfast-style plate of fried bacon strips, roasted diced potatoes, and cubed honeydew/cantaloupe-type melon.

STEP 2 - Vessel: A pale green dinner plate, roughly 26 cm in diameter. Area = 3.14 x 13^2 ≈ 530 cm^2. The melon at the top right edge appears to sit on the same plate, so it is included.

STEP 3 - Items:
- Bacon strips (cooked, crisp)
- Roasted potato cubes (with some browning and seasoning)
- Melon cubes (pale green, likely honeydew)

STEP 4 - Area (percent of plate):
- Bacon: ~20% (about 106 cm^2)
- Potatoes: ~17% (about 90 cm^2)
- Melon: ~13% (about 69 cm^2)
Total covered ≈ 50%, which is a plausible share of the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume (area x typical height):
- Bacon: 106 cm^2 x 0.5 cm ≈ 53 ml (flat strips, low height)
- Potatoes: 90 cm^2 x 2 cm ≈ 180 ml
- Melon: 69 cm^2 x 2 cm ≈ 138 ml

STEP 6 - Grams (bulk density):
- Bacon: 53 ml x 0.9 ≈ 48 g
- Potatoes: 180 ml x 0.7 ≈ 126 g (diced cooked potato is fairly dense, but with gaps between pieces)
- Melon: 138 ml x 0.6 ≈ 83 g

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Bacon, cooked: 48 g x 540 kcal/100 g ≈ 259 kcal
- Roasted potatoes: 126 g x 130 kcal/100 g ≈ 164 kcal (roasting likely with a little oil, but none is clearly visible beyond a light sheen, so I keep it modest)
- Melon: 83 g x 34 kcal/100 g ≈ 28 kcal

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Total ≈ 257 g and ≈ 451 kcal. For a half-covered 26 cm plate with three components, this is plausible. Bacon and potatoes dominate the energy, as expected.
